    Many ad networks at once

    Industry opt-out pages. They work by setting cookies, so repeat them if you clear your cookies.

    • Your Online Choices (UK and EU) (opens in a new tab)
    • YourAdChoices (US) (opens in a new tab)

    Stop apps on your phone tracking you

    Apps share an advertising ID that links what you do across apps. Switch it off in a minute.

    iPhone and iPad Your device

    1. Open Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Tracking.
    2. Turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track".

    Android Your device

    1. Open Settings, then Privacy, then Ads. On some phones it is Settings, then Google, then Ads.
    2. Tap "Delete advertising ID" and confirm.

    Save your results

    Keep a copy to compare after you change your settings or switch browsers. It stays on your device.

    Questions

    Does Ad Mirror collect or store my data?

    No. Ad Mirror has no server, no cookies and no analytics. Everything on this page is worked out by your own browser and disappears when you close the tab.

    You can check this yourself: the badge at the top counts every request this page makes to another server. It stays at zero unless you run the server check.

    What is a device fingerprint?

    It is an ID built from the small details of your device: your screen, graphics chip, fonts, and how your device draws images. Each detail is common, but the combination is often rare enough to pick you out.

    Unlike a cookie, there is nothing stored on your device to delete. That is why it survives clearing cookies and private windows.

    Do advertisers really use fingerprints?

    Yes. Since 16 February 2025, Google has allowed advertisers on its platforms to use fingerprinting. The UK's data protection regulator called the change "irresponsible" and warned it "could now replace the functions of third-party cookies".

    Google also decided in 2025 to keep third-party cookies in Chrome, so cookie tracking continues too.

    Read the regulator's statement (opens in a new tab)

    Isn't a private window enough?

    A private window deletes cookies and history when you close it. Your fingerprint and IP address stay the same, so sites can often still recognise you. An ad blocker and a browser that scrambles fingerprints protect you much more.

    Why does the server check share my IP address?

    To find out whether your browser blocks an ad server, we have to try to contact it, and any server you contact sees your IP address. This happens every time you visit a site with ads. We only run the check when you ask, and we send no cookies or other details.

    Will an ad blocker break websites?

    Rarely. Most sites work normally and load faster. If one does not, you can pause the blocker for that site with one click. Some news sites ask you to turn it off or subscribe.

    Who makes Ad Mirror?

    Ad Mirror is an independent project. It is not linked to any advertiser or ad company. The code is public, so anyone can check what it does.
